results.content: From 2003 to 2008 I coordinated the**NSF/University of Arizona IGERT Program in Archaeological Sciences**, which has so far produced 28 PhDs. My earlier research was mostly in archaeometallurgy, and in Africa, but since 2009 has been mostly on the provenance of archaeological materials worldwide. I provide the expertise in optical petrography for studies of the provenance of low-fired pottery in Botswana, New Caledonia and the southwestern USA, and collaborate with isotope geochemist Joaquin Ruiz, and with current and former PhD advisees, to use lead and strontium isotopes for provenance of non-ferrous metals, turquoise, and lead glazes in the southwestern USA and in Africa.
